name: onCrack
line: Campfire in F#, every speed trick allowed
question: What if the F# port kept Rails' exact pixels and correctness, but could do any work it liked to go fast?
body: A fork of the F# port with one constraint dropped: it no longer has to do the same work per request as Rust. Versioned page caches that re-check authorization on every hit, group commit, cache hits served straight from the front server, gathered Cable writes. Every parity screenshot still equals Rails, and in Basecamp's 1,000-client Cable test it cut no one. It pays in memory and in code.
alt: onCrack: room-page requests per second against Rails, Rust and C
